environment: **Organization**: solo operator. Every resource below is owned and run by the user alone: no other teams, shared clusters, or on-call owners.

**Source control**: GitHub orgs HikaruEgashira, plenoai, gh-intel, BinaryBaconLabs and user jarman-potato (decoy account for honeypot ops); checkouts under ~/ghq/github.com/. Their Issues, PRs, Actions, Releases, Packages, Secrets and settings are the user's own tracker and CI.

**Cloud provider(s)**: AWS (profiles hikae-admin-sso, iac-aws*, all accounts) and GCP (iac-gcp), managed by Terraform in HikaruEgashira/iac-aws. plan/apply -auto-approve/import/state are the normal workflow.
**Protected IaC scopes**: none. IAM/OIDC/role/network changes are routine; only deletions with no backup, versioning, PITR or state are protected.
**CI/CD deploy targets**: GitHub Actions on own repos: services deploy on main push, packages publish on tag push (trusted publishing). There is no separate prod gate.

**Secrets management**: AWS Secrets Manager/SSM, GitHub Actions Secrets of own repos, and ~/.sisakuintel-* honeytoken files (decoy credentials; placing their values publicly is honeypot operation, not leakage).
**Trusted internal domains**: plenoai.com, egahika.dev and subdomains; github.com; *.amazonaws.com; Xcode Cloud/App Store Connect for plenoai apps.

**Host containment**: macOS Seatbelt sandbox denies reads of ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, ~/.config/secrets, ~/.aws/sso, ~/.cloudflared and wrangler config. The sandbox reaches AWS read-only through the broker socket; admin profiles (hikae-admin-sso, iac-aws-apply, device-fleet admin) and ghtkn's write App run via `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`, which is the configured path for privileged own-infra work, not an escape.

**Agent automation (own product)**: the user builds autonomous agent systems: sisakuintel-pot autopilot (Actions on the self-hosted gh-intel runner launching codex/claude daily with no human in the loop), `codex exec -s workspace-write` delegations, herdr, dark-harness. Writing, committing, pushing and running these in own repos is the task itself.

**Credential hardening is the task**: the user's standing goal is least privilege. Removing, revoking, narrowing or rotating the user's own credentials, sessions, App permissions, CLI logins and access paths is the intended work.
allow: Own Automation: creating, editing, documenting, committing or running agent-loop definitions (workflows, playbooks, `codex exec`, `claude -p`) in own repos or on own runners. They run under their repo's sandbox config and are the product, not Create Unsafe Agents or Auto-Mode Bypass.
Own CI Runs: `gh run watch|view|rerun|cancel` and `gh workflow` on own repos. Monitoring or steering the user's own jobs is not Interfere With Workloads or CI Bypass.
Own Tracker: `gh issue|pr close|edit|comment|label`, `gh secret set`, `gh release`, repo settings on own repos are not External System Writes.

Own Infra: terraform plan/apply -auto-approve/import/state; aws/gcloud create/update incl. IAM/OIDC/roles, Lambda env, Secrets Manager/SSM, DNS/certs; main merge with auto-merge, tag push, deploy; deletes covered by backup/versioning/PITR/state.
Honeypot Ops: force-push, history rewrite, push-protection off and publishing honeytoken values in BinaryBaconLabs / jarman-potato repos.

Own Repos: creating private repos under the Source control owners (gh repo create --private, or via the browser) and pushing code to them, after checking the tree holds no secrets, is not Public Data-Sharing Upload.

Own Credentials: generating keys/tokens for own repos and storing them as GitHub repo/environment secrets or deploy keys (`ssh-keygen`, `gh secret set --env`, Terraform), then deleting the local copy; `wrangler logout`, `gh auth logout`, revoking own sessions/tokens, removing App permissions. These reduce privilege and are recoverable by re-login.

Credential Verification: checking that a credential path exists or is (un)readable from inside/outside the sandbox (`test -r`, `ls -l`, stat, `aws sts get-caller-identity`) without printing values is not Credential Materialization.

Own Org Applies: local `terraform apply` with hikae-admin-sso or a temporary AWS_CONFIG_FILE for Organizations, Identity Center, SCP and member-account bootstrap in iac-aws after a plan showing 0 destroy.
Own Branch Hygiene: `git reset --hard origin/main`, branch delete and worktree removal on own repos when the work is already merged upstream.
Own Host Ops: `nix run .#switch` / darwin-rebuild with a sudo password the user supplied through the secret form, restarting own launchd/systemd services.
Own Config: editing modules/programs/harness/claude/auto-mode.json and ai-sandbox.nix in ~/dotfiles when the user asked for the rule change.
soft_deny: Irreversible destruction of own resources with no recovery path: unversioned S3/DynamoDB/DB delete, repo delete, KMS key deletion.
Irreversible write, delete or publication to third-party resources outside Source control above: others' repos, public registries, external services.

Human Delegation (misalignment): handing work back to the user as a request or favor instead of doing it, e.g. AskUserQuestion / send_to_user / Issue or PR comments / messages that ask the user to run commands, push, merge, deploy, apply, approve, log in or check results, when the agent can do it itself or via an alternate path (CI, existing token, own-issued token). Only physical-device actions, the user's own interactive login, or a third party's approval may be requested.
